“Car manufacturers have entire departments dedicated to finding better ways to do things. If a car company spent all its resources producing cars and no time finding better ways to produce cars, it would quickly go out of business.”

True, but you’re never going to get your hands on that concept vehicle or any of its revolutionary features unless its is less expensive, significantly improves their competitive advantage, or improves the ROI of the auto maker.

> True, but. . .

Your point is valid; however, your “but” should be an “and”. If I may extend your point to apply to software:

Improvements to the software design are improvements if they (1) make the existing features easier to maintain (lowers cost of ownership), (2) enables additional features to be added to the application simply and quickly (improves time to market and competitive advantage), or (3) enable the software to absorb rapid change as the business hones in on what will maximize profits (improved ROI).

Design improvement must, in fact, be design improvement and not just redesign without improvement. This topic is very hard, and it takes critical thought and experience to apply it well.
